label: Account named in multiple complaints
description: An account named as the suspected beneficiary in several independent cybercrime complaints. The strongest signal the platform holds, because it comes from outside the transaction data: a complaint is a person reporting a loss, not a pattern inferred from a ledger.
confounders: A large merchant will accumulate complaints simply by having many customers, some of whom dispute charges. Complaint count has to be read against transaction volume.
A single incident reported by several victims is several complaints about one event, not several events.
A misattributed complaint: the victim names the account they can see, which may be an intermediary rather than the beneficiary.
notes: These correlations are tier 1, meaning the complaint named the account directly. That is an identity match and carries no confidence score, because it is not a probabilistic claim — the reference either matches or it does not. Tiers 3 to 5 are inferences and do carry confidence plus a review state. Conflating the two is the single most consequential presentation error in this part of the product: an inferred link shown as certain is how an investigation ends up aimed at the wrong person.
